newsitem.title: UK: TENNIS-DEFENDING CHAMPION SELES BEATEN IN EASTBOURNE.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-DEFENDING CHAMPION SELES BEATEN IN EASTBOURNE.

text.p: Defending champion Monica Seles was knocked out of the Eastbourne women's grasscourt tournament in a quarter-final match which began on Thursday and ended on Saturday.

The top-seeded American and world number two was beaten 7-5 7-5 by big-serving Dutchwoman Brenda Schultz-McCarthy, the eighth seed, and then admitted that she had some work to do on her game before Wimbledon next week.

"I am going to try to get my serve a little bit more in order because I think this week it really has let me down," said Seles, who was 5-2 up in the first set on Thursday before letting the match slip through her fingers.
Rain halted the match at 2-2 in the second set on Thursday and washed out all hope of resuming it on Friday.

When it did restart in blustery conditions on Saturday Seles broke to go 4-2 up but was broken straight back and then conceded another break with a double fault, leaving Schultz-McCarthy to serve out for the match to love, finishing with an ace.
Seles said she was missing the support of her father and coach Karolj, who has cancer, but spoke to him every day by telephone.
"There are other people I can turn to but I wish my dad was here," she said.
In the semifinals later on Saturday Schultz-McCarthy will play fourth seed Arantxa Sanchez Vicario who beat sixth seeded Romanian Irina Spirlea, winning 6-4 6-4.
Second seed Jana Novotna had a harder time gaining her place in the last four in a match interrupted by rain on Friday when the Czech was leading 6-2 6-5 against Japan's Ai Sugiyama.

The match resumed at 15-15, with Novotna needing only three more points for victory. But swirling winds and Novotna's own tendency to collapse at important moments kept the two players on court another 46 minutes before the Czech won 6-2 6-7 6-4.
Novotna failed to convert a matchpoint and then double-faulted to concede the break which took the second set to a tiebreak, won 8-6 by Sugiyama.
In the third set she gave away another break on a double fault but pulled back to go 5-4 ahead and then took advantage of a run of errors by the Japanese to sew up the match.
She now plays Natasha Zvereva of Belarus who beat Frenchwoman Nathalie Tauziat 6-4 5-7 6-4 in another rain-interrupted quarter-final.
Organisers were hoping to cram in both semifinals and the final on Saturday, to give the players their traditional day off before Wimbledon begins on Monday.
